scenario.title: Mars: The Voice Beyond the Ridge
scenario.premise: A damaged landing strands a small expedition. Recovery becomes a rescue, then a return journey carrying people and evidence. This is an engineering story with recovered qualified systems, not real survival instructions.

stage.title: A voice above the ridge
stage.speaker: Mission Control
stage.motivation: We lost your signal on landing. Repair the radio and put a powered signal above the ridge. We are listening.
stage.travelText: We take the useful equipment onward to a voice above the ridge, leaving the earlier work where it stands.

args: Started fresh at Weather with authored baseline 43 attempts and 38 combinations excluded. Completed Weather and advanced to Relay: my delta is 20 attempts, 14 accepted, 13 combinations, 1 advance, 6 failed combinations, 4 hints. Mast plus vane and rotor install were intuitive; station becoming functional then producing a weather record and updating the map gave a coherent payoff. Most sensor preparation and installation felt like checklist work. Empty logger, temperature and pressure slots invited direct matching items, but each failed with only No new combination here. Logger wiring was inferable; thermometer louver and pressure housing needed hints. Sealed housing plus controller also failed; mesh plus housing then controller worked. Object descriptions explain combinations afterward instead of supplying useful clues beforehand. Sources remain on the board after creations, adding clutter and making parts feel duplicable. At Relay the missing crew invitation is appealing but another large maintenance cabinet suggests repetition, so I voluntarily stop rather than pursue completion. Logical agent play only, not human fun evidence. Read instructions and player output only, no scenario or source inspection.
